spec.description: Hourly NO2 at GGD Amsterdam's 17 reference stations, from Luchtmeetnet, with a surface between them; reloaded every 15 minutes.

options.content:
### Where the data comes from

[Luchtmeetnet](https://www.luchtmeetnet.nl/) is the Dutch national air quality network, run by RIVM with the GGDs and the provinces. Its stations are reference instruments, the kind a city's compliance is measured with, and it publishes their readings hour by hour as open data, through [its API](https://api-docs.luchtmeetnet.nl/).

This dashboard reads the 17 stations of GGD Amsterdam's network that measure nitrogen dioxide (NO2), from Zaandam in the north to Oude Meer by Schiphol in the south. Each value is the mean of one hour, published within about an hour of its end; the dashboard reloads every 15 minutes. The latest hours are provisional: the network validates its data later, and a value can still change.

The requests go through Grafana's server and a cache, one per station, and ask for whole hours, so every visitor in the same hour shares one copy. The time range picks the hours, up to its last 7 days, the most the API gives in one request.

### How to read it

- **NO2** is in µg/m³. It comes mostly from road traffic, so it is highest beside busy roads and in the rush hours, and it changes from one street to the next: that is why the map shows it. Particulate matter (PM10, PM2.5) travels far and varies little across one city; the selected station's panel has it.
- The colours are 5 bands, from dim to bright: brighter is more NO2. The brightest is above 25 µg/m³, the WHO 2021 guideline for a 24-hour mean (the dashed lines); the WHO's for a year's mean is 10 µg/m³; the EU's limit for a year's mean is 40 µg/m³, and 20 µg/m³ from 2030.
- A mean needs 75% of its hours: 18 for the last 24 hours, the EU's rule for a daily mean. A station short of them is left out of the ranking and the surface.
- A reading a little under zero, the instruments' noise around nothing, counts as 0.

### The map

The cards are the stations' hourly NO2 over the time range, all on one scale; a station with no room for a card stays as a dot, and one that stops reporting turns red. Under them, a surface interpolated between the stations (inverse distance weighting, over the area they span) of each station's mean in the window of the **time filter** at the foot of the map. The window opens on the whole range; narrowed to an hour and played, the surface redraws hour by hour, and each card's cursor and value follow it. The surface is a guess between 17 points, not a measurement: a station by a busy road raises the guess around it, though the street behind may be cleaner.

### How it works

Grafana's DuckDB fetches the readings, and hands them to DuckDB running in your browser (the Chaski data source), which answers every panel and every click without another round trip. The map is the Kepler Geospatial Maps Plus panel, with its Sparkline and Surface layers; the ranking is Business Charts (Apache ECharts).

spec.rawSql:
WITH latest AS (SELECT max(time) AS t FROM $series),
span AS (SELECT greatest(date_diff('hour', min(time), max(time)) + 1, 1) AS hours FROM $series),
per AS (
  SELECT station, any_value(name) AS name, any_value(kind) AS kind,
         any_value(latitude) AS latitude, any_value(longitude) AS longitude,
         max(time) AS last_time,
         arg_max(no2, time) AS last_no2,
         avg(no2) FILTER (WHERE time > latest.t - INTERVAL 24 HOUR) AS mean_24h,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE time > latest.t - INTERVAL 24 HOUR) AS hours_24h,
         avg(no2) AS mean_range,
         max(no2) AS max_range,
         count(*) AS hours_range
  FROM $series, latest
  GROUP BY station
)
SELECT station, name, kind, round(mean_24h, 1) AS mean_24h, round(last_no2, 1) AS last_no2
FROM per
WHERE hours_24h >= 18
ORDER BY mean_24h DESC

spec.description: Each station's mean NO2 over the last 24 hours of data (with at least 18 of them), in the map's colours; the tick is its latest hour. The dashed line is the WHO 2021 guideline for a 24-hour mean, 25 µg/m³. Click a bar to pick the station; click it again to clear it.
spec.title: Stations, last 24 hours

spec.rawSql:
WITH latest AS (SELECT max(time) AS t FROM $series)
SELECT count(DISTINCT station) AS "Stations"
FROM $series, latest
WHERE time >= latest.t - INTERVAL 1 HOUR

spec.rawSql:
WITH latest AS (SELECT max(time) AS t FROM $series),
span AS (SELECT greatest(date_diff('hour', min(time), max(time)) + 1, 1) AS hours FROM $series),
per AS (
  SELECT station, any_value(name) AS name, any_value(kind) AS kind,
         any_value(latitude) AS latitude, any_value(longitude) AS longitude,
         max(time) AS last_time,
         arg_max(no2, time) AS last_no2,
         avg(no2) FILTER (WHERE time > latest.t - INTERVAL 24 HOUR) AS mean_24h,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE time > latest.t - INTERVAL 24 HOUR) AS hours_24h,
         avg(no2) AS mean_range,
         max(no2) AS max_range,
         count(*) AS hours_range
  FROM $series, latest
  GROUP BY station
),
facts AS (
  SELECT [
    ('Station', name), ('Code', station), ('Type', kind),
    ('Latest hour', coalesce(last_no2 || ' µg/m³', 'no reading')),
    ('24 h mean', coalesce(round(mean_24h, 1) || ' µg/m³', 'too few hours')),
    ('Range mean', round(mean_range, 1) || ' µg/m³'),
    ('Range max', max_range || ' µg/m³'),
    ('Hours with a reading', hours_range::VARCHAR),
    ('Last reading (UTC)', strftime(last_time, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'))
  ] AS f
  FROM per
  WHERE station = $station
)
SELECT unnest(f, recursive := true) FROM facts

WITH latest AS (SELECT max(time) AS t FROM $series),
span AS (SELECT greatest(date_diff('hour', min(time), max(time)) + 1, 1) AS hours FROM $series),
per AS (
  SELECT station, any_value(name) AS name, any_value(kind) AS kind,
         any_value(latitude) AS latitude, any_value(longitude) AS longitude,
         max(time) AS last_time,
         arg_max(no2, time) AS last_no2,
         avg(no2) FILTER (WHERE time > latest.t - INTERVAL 24 HOUR) AS mean_24h,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE time > latest.t - INTERVAL 24 HOUR) AS hours_24h,
         avg(no2) AS mean_range,
         max(no2) AS max_range,
         count(*) AS hours_range
  FROM $series, latest
  GROUP BY station
)
SELECT name AS "Station", kind AS "Type",
       last_no2 AS "Latest hour", round(mean_24h, 1) AS "24 h mean", round(mean_range, 1) AS "Range mean",
       max_range AS "Range max", hours_range AS "Hours",
       strftime(last_time, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') AS "Last reading (UTC)"
FROM per
ORDER BY mean_24h DESC NULLS LAST

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: the hourly NO2 of GGD Amsterdam's 17 stations over the time
-- range (at most its last 7 days), from Luchtmeetnet's open API, one request per
-- station, through the gateway's cache (feeds). Each value is the mean of the
-- hour that ends at its time. A reading a little under zero (the instruments'
-- noise around nothing) counts as 0.
WITH stations(station, name, kind, latitude, longitude) AS (VALUES
  ('NL49002', 'Haarlemmerweg', 'Traffic', 52.38542, 4.87575),
  ('NL49003', 'Nieuwendammerdijk', 'Municipal', 52.38931, 4.94382),
  ('NL49007', 'Einsteinweg', 'Traffic', 52.38133, 4.84523),
  ('NL49012', 'Van Diemenstraat', 'Traffic', 52.38998, 4.88781),
  ('NL49014', 'Vondelpark', 'Municipal', 52.35971, 4.86621),
  ('NL49017', 'Stadhouderskade', 'Traffic', 52.35804, 4.89970),
  ('NL49019', 'Oude Schans', 'Municipal', 52.37206, 4.90440),
  ('NL49020', 'Jan van Galenstraat', 'Traffic', 52.37479, 4.86032),
  ('NL49021', 'Kantershof', 'Municipal', 52.32069, 4.98840),
  ('NL49022', 'Ookmeer', 'Municipal', 52.36681, 4.79334),
  ('NL49546', 'Zaanstad-Hemkade', 'Industrial', 52.42023, 4.83206),
  ('NL49561', 'Badhoevedorp-Sloterweg', 'Other', 52.33400, 4.77401),
  ('NL49564', 'Hoofddorp-Hoofdweg', 'Other', 52.32745, 4.71507),
  ('NL49565', 'Oude Meer-Aalsmeerderdijk', 'Regional', 52.28013, 4.77082),
  ('NL49701', 'Zaandam-Wagenschotpad', 'Municipal', 52.44801, 4.81671),
  ('NL49703', 'Spaarnwoude-Machineweg', 'Regional', 52.39844, 4.72858),
  ('NL49704', 'Zaanstad-Hoogtij', 'Industrial', 52.42800, 4.77300)
),
span AS (
  -- Whole hours, so one URL stands for an hour and the gateway's cache can
  -- answer it; and at most 7 days, the most Luchtmeetnet gives in one request.
  SELECT date_trunc('hour', make_timestamp(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) * 1000)) AS t1,
         greatest(date_trunc('hour', make_timestamp(CAST(${__from} AS BIGINT) * 1000)), t1 - INTERVAL 7 DAY) AS t0
),
fetched AS (
  SELECT s.*, http_get('http://feeds/luchtmeetnet/measurements?station_number=' || station || '&formula=' || 'NO2' || '&start=' || strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:00:00Z') || '&end=' || strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:00:00Z')) AS r
  FROM stations AS s, span
),
readings AS (
  SELECT station, name, kind, latitude, longitude, unnest(from_json((r->>'body')::JSON->'data', '[{"timestamp_measured":"VARCHAR","value":"DOUBLE"}]')) AS m
  FROM fetched
  WHERE (r->>'status') = '200'
)
SELECT station, name, kind, latitude, longitude,
       m.timestamp_measured::TIMESTAMPTZ AS time,
       round(greatest(m.value, 0), 1) AS no2
FROM readings
WHERE m.value IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY station, time

-- Server side: every pollutant the station clicked on the map measures, hourly,
-- over the same hours as the map. Nothing is fetched until one is clicked.
WITH formulas(formula, pollutant) AS (VALUES ('NO2', 'NO2'), ('PM10', 'PM10'), ('PM25', 'PM2.5'), ('O3', 'O3')),
span AS (
  -- Whole hours, so one URL stands for an hour and the gateway's cache can
  -- answer it; and at most 7 days, the most Luchtmeetnet gives in one request.
  SELECT date_trunc('hour', make_timestamp(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) * 1000)) AS t1,
         greatest(date_trunc('hour', make_timestamp(CAST(${__from} AS BIGINT) * 1000)), t1 - INTERVAL 7 DAY) AS t0
),
fetched AS (
  SELECT pollutant, http_get('http://feeds/luchtmeetnet/measurements?station_number=' || '${station:raw}' || '&formula=' || formula || '&start=' || strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:00:00Z') || '&end=' || strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:00:00Z')) AS r
  FROM formulas, span
  WHERE regexp_full_match('${station:raw}', 'NL[0-9]{5}')
),
readings AS (
  SELECT pollutant, unnest(from_json((r->>'body')::JSON->'data', '[{"timestamp_measured":"VARCHAR","value":"DOUBLE"}]')) AS m
  FROM fetched
  WHERE (r->>'status') = '200'
)
SELECT pollutant, m.timestamp_measured::TIMESTAMPTZ AS time, round(greatest(m.value, 0), 1) AS value
FROM readings
WHERE m.value IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY pollutant, time
